# claude.md - Register Errands - VI Dynamic (tree 756760393)

## Purpose
ETG (eTraveli Group) SUBTREE of "Register Errands - Dynamic" (tree 595124299), for the
Self Transfer Guarantee / Virtual Interlining (VI) contact reasons. It collects the VI
eligibility + disruption details, the STG offer the agent made, the Edvin type and the
customer action, and hands ONE combined-PNR errand record back to the parent tree, which
owns all Zendesk ticket creation, the internal note and the Edvin registration.

Entered from the parent tree's node 76 (Tree node, open_tree_id 756760393,
open_tree_node_id 0 -> this tree's root, return_tree_node_id 3). The parent reaches it from
its node 75 "Is VI Selection", which matches custom_field_29658558478738 against
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi,
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi_sc and
contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi_passengers_at_the_airport.
This tree exits at node 79 (Tree node, "Return Parent", open_tree_id 1 = return to the
calling tree); the parent resumes at its node 3 (any child tickets?) -> child/silent/
grandchild loop -> 21 internal note -> 22 -> 44 Edvin registration loop.

## Architecture (flow)
```
83 Set VI Combined PNR   (ROOT - collapses the selected PNRs into one record, resets VI state)
  -> 48 partner selection            [dropdown: partner, date: orderCreated]
  -> 82 Partner / order-age route    (sets form data `route`)
  -> 49 Partner logic                (route == "50" -> 50, else -> 66)
       50 Bcom OR ETG & prior 21May26      66 ETG & post 22may2026
       [dropdowns: disruption_type, delay_reason (Trip delay), flight_affected (Schedule*)]
  -> 52 (from 50) / 67 (from 66) route on disruption + flight:
       Schedule change (within/outside 24h) -> 53 (Booking) / 69 (ETG)
       Trip delay                           -> 62 (Booking) / 73 (ETG)
       Accomodation / Meal compensation     -> 80
  STG offer ladder - each screen exits to 80 when an offer is taken, or falls to the next:
       Booking: 53 -> 58 -> {80 | 59} ; 59 -> 60 -> {80 | 61} ; 61 -> 80
                62 -> 63 -> {80 | 64} ; 64 -> 65 -> {80 | 61}
       ETG:     69 -> 70 -> {80 | 71} ; 71 -> 72 -> {80 | 61}
                73 -> 74 -> {80 | 75} ; 75 -> 76 -> {80 | 61}
  -> 80 Get Errand Configurations  (Data node, CO 182 + 183)
  -> 81 Format Types               (channel/category + types_list/actions_by_type/...)
  -> 1  Agent - Select Channel & Type  [select: type (dynamic from category.types), notes]
  -> 2  Dynamic Actions List Options   (actions_array, VI details, records the combined PNR)
  -> 12 Create PNR Action Table -> 25 Display PNR Action Table  (agent picks the action)
  -> 27 Stitch & Group  -> 84 Set VI Finals (combined PNR) -> 79 Return Parent
```
Node 5 is this claude.md - unlinked, never in the flow.

## Data dictionary
- transforms.selected_pnrs: the order-grid rows the agent picked, set by the PARENT tree's
  node 24 from views.findorder. INPUT to this tree.
- transforms.current_pnr: THE COMBINED PNR record. Built by node 83 from selected_pnrs
  (pnr = every selected PNR joined with ", "), enriched by node 2 (channel, category, type,
  notes, vi_details, actions_array), resolved by node 27 (customer_action, bucket, bucketId,
  actionId), and republished by node 84 as the final record.
- transforms.combined_pnr_record / transforms.combined_pnr: the node 83 baseline record and
  the joined PNR string. combined_pnr is mirrored as form data.
- transforms.channel / transforms.category: Edvin channel + category OBJECTS, resolved by
  node 81 from actions.edvin__errand_configuration and actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value.
  This tree fetches its own config at node 80 - it no longer depends on the parent's node 46.
- transforms.types_list / types_by_id / actions_by_type / actions_by_type_name /
  actions_flat: node 81's groupings. actions_by_type["<typeId>"] is what node 2 reads, and
  category.types is the dynamic list source behind node 1's `type` select.
- transforms.actions_array: the normalized actions for the selected type, taken from
  actions_by_type. Item shape {id, name, bucket (STRING routing key), bucketId, actionId,
  edvin_actions, type_id, type_name}.
- transforms.customer_action_pnrs: the customer-action rows the table on nodes 12/25
  renders. On the VI path this holds exactly ONE row - the combined PNR. Upserted by pnr in
  node 2, restitched in node 27, replaced with the final record in node 84. The parent's
  node 21 prints the internal note from this list.
- transforms.vi_details / transforms.vi_details_text: the VI/STG answers as an object and as
  printable text. Captured in node 2, stored on the record, and folded into the record's
  `notes` so the parent prints them in the internal note (its node 21, "Notes") and in the
  Edvin errand free text (its node 44, "Agent Notes") with no parent-side change.
- transforms.child_tickets: [{child_ticket:{... grandchild_tickets:[]}}]. Built node 27 by
  grouping the stitched rows on the DISTINCT (type + customer_action) key. Consumed by the
  parent's node 32 loop.
- transforms.final_pnrs: THE hand-off. Exactly ONE entry on the VI path (the combined PNR),
  written by node 84. The parent's node 44 registers one Edvin errand per entry.
- transforms.unresolved_selections + has_unresolved_selections /
  unresolved_selections_count (form data): node 27 diagnostics for a customer action it
  could not resolve to an (action, known bucket) pair. Recorded and logged only - this tree
  has no re-pick screen yet. See Open items.
- Form-data scalars published by node 84 for logic nodes and Connected Objects:
  combined_pnr, customer_action, customer_action_id, bucket, bucket_id, errand_type,
  stg_outcome, stg_trail. `type` is deliberately NOT overwritten - it holds the Edvin type ID that node
  1's select and node 2's lookup depend on.
- Record fields that follow the v5 hand-off contract (node 118 of
  "Register Errands - VI Dynamic (v5 subtree-only 2026-08-20).json") so the two designs stay
  interchangeable: pnr (joined), postSaleHandleType / providerSystem (joined with " / "),
  id + providerPnrIds (FLAT array of provider booking ids), vi_pnr_count, and the flattened
  partner / disruption_type / delay_reason / flight_affected / stg_outcome. Node 84 also
  builds providerBookingIds itself, as JSON.stringify of the FLAT, de-duped id array - the
  parent's node 27 builds it as JSON.stringify(group.map(i => i.id)), which nests on a
  collapsed record because `id` is already an array. It reads the FIRST source that has ids
  (providerPnrIds, then id, then the node 83 baseline), never a concatenation of all three -
  they all hold the same ids, so concatenating triples the list.
- transforms.isMorePNR is set false by nodes 83 and 84, so the collapsed record can never be
  routed into the parent's per-PNR loop (its node 11) whichever node the parent returns
  through.
- route / order_created_date (form data): node 82's routing scalar and the date it resolved.
- stg_outcome / stg_trail (form data + record fields, node 84): the STG ladder is walked
  top-down and every rung the agent could not fill answers "None of the above is available",
  so the OUTCOME is the LAST rung that named a real offer - not the first answer found. All
  declines means the outcome genuinely is "None of the above is available". stg_trail keeps
  every answer in ladder order, joined with " -> ", for the note.
- VI selection variables (form data, cleared by node 83 on entry): partner, orderCreated,
  route, disruption_type, delay_reason, flight_affected, stg_alternatives_sameday_sc,
  stg_alternatives_overnight_sc, stg_alternatives_sameday_td, stg_alternatives_overnight_td,
  stg_refund.

## External systems (CX Actions / Connected Objects)
- Node 80 "Get Errand Configurations" - Data node, org 116, CO **182** and **183**, producing
  actions.edvin__errand_configuration and actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value.
- Nothing else in this tree calls an API. Every Zendesk and Edvin WRITE happens in the
  parent tree after node 79 returns.

## Conventions & gotchas
- ONE COMBINED PNR, ONE ERRAND. VI is a self-transfer itinerary: the PNRs are legs of the
  same journey, so they collapse into a single record (node 83) and produce a single Edvin
  errand and a single child/silent ticket. Do not reintroduce the parent tree's per-PNR loop
  (its nodes 7/11) here.
- ONE PRODUCER OF BUCKET KEYS. Edvin returns bucket as {id, name} where `name` is a HUMAN
  LABEL ("No action", "Proceed", "Different request"), not the snake_case key this workflow
  routes on. Node 81 maps it ID-first (BUCKET_BY_ID {3: no_action, 4: proceed,
  5: different_request}), name map as fallback, unmapped returned UNCHANGED and never
  guessed. **Node 2 reads node 81's actions_by_type rather than re-mapping** - it used to
  keep its own label-only copy, which is exactly why every bucket except "Proceed" reached
  node 27 unusable. Node 2 still carries the same block as a fallback for a session where
  node 81 has not run; if you ever edit one, edit both.
- GROUPING KEY: distinct errand = (type + customer_action) TOGETHER, never action alone.
  proceed -> ONE active child ticket (grandchildren one per distinct pair, only when 2+
  pairs); non-proceed -> ONE silent ticket per distinct pair; Edvin -> one errand per pair.
  On the VI path there is one row, so this always resolves to one ticket and one errand -
  but the code is shared with the parent's contract, so do not "simplify" it away.
- ACTION RESOLUTION IS ID-OR-NAME. Node 12 currently renders action NAMES as its option
  values; node 27 matches actionId, then id, then name, so either render resolves. If node
  12 is ever hardened to emit action IDs (the parent tree's v29 build), node 27 needs no
  change.
- keep_vars_on_back = 1. It was 0, so any Back navigation through the VI screens discarded
  the captured values - an independent way to lose the customer action and its bucket. The
  parent tree hit the same thing and fixed it the same way (its v26).
- Node 83 clears the VI selection variables on entry because form data never expires. A
  second contact in the same session would otherwise inherit the previous disruption/STG
  answers, and a conditional field that is no longer shown would still post its old value.
- THE CUTOFF COMPARE IS DATE-ONLY AND TIMEZONE-FREE (node 82). `new Date('2026-05-21T00:00:00')`
  parses as LOCAL midnight while Edvin's orderCreated is an ISO timestamp, so a late-20-May
  order could fall either side depending on where the engine runs. Node 82 compares
  YYYY-MM-DD prefixes as strings instead. It prefers the agent-entered `orderCreated` on
  node 48, then the API value, and logs a warning when neither is readable (route then falls
  back to "66"). BOUNDARY: an order created ON 2026-05-21 routes to node 66 - unchanged from
  the original, but node 50 is titled "prior 21May26" and 66 "post 22may2026", so the 21st
  itself is not described by either. Confirm with ETG.
- THE STG OPTION STRINGS ARE THE CONTRACT. Every alternatives screen is followed by a logic
  node comparing the selected value to the exact option text, so an edited option label must
  be edited in BOTH places. Trailing spaces are silent killers: node 71's first option used
  to end in a space and node 72's expression did not, so that branch fell through to its
  default (button_link 0, a dead end).
- Selections are DROPDOWNS (native `select` formfields), not radios, as of 2026-08-21 (v7).
  Each keeps its original variable name so every logic expression still matches. Static
  option lists with {"filterable":true}; none are `required`, because a required field that
  a conditional hides can block the node.
- EVERY CONVERTED DROPDOWN LEADS WITH A "- Select -" PLACEHOLDER. A radio starts with
  nothing chosen; a select can hand back its first option even when the agent never touched
  it, which would silently default `partner` to "Booking" and route the contact down the
  wrong partner's STG rules. "- Select -" matches no logic expression, so an unanswered
  screen falls to the same default branch it did as a radio. Drop the placeholder ONLY after
  confirming in sandbox that Zingtree renders its own blank first option for a static
  select - and if you do, re-check node 49 and every *_logic node for what an unanswered
  screen now does.
- No persistent button. persist_names / persist_node_ids used to point at node 29 (Clear
  Data), which no longer exists in this tree; both are now empty. If you add one, point it
  at a node that exists.

## Open items
0. **Fixed here, but the same hole is still in the PARENT tree**: `bucketKey()` in the
   parent's nodes 2 and 46 dereferences `b.id` with no null guard, so a single Edvin action
   with a missing bucket throws and takes the whole node down. Node 81 here now returns ""
   for a null bucket (which node 27 then flags as bucket_missing, the correct outcome).
   Worth the one-line fix on the parent next time it is touched.
1. **The bare contact reason crashes node 81.** The parent's node 75 routes
   contact_reason_sc__self_transfer_guarantee_vi (the parent value) into this tree, but
   CONTACT_REASON_BY_ZENDESK only maps the two leaf values (`_vi_sc`,
   `_vi_passengers_at_the_airport`), so that contact throws at node 81. The node now logs the
   Zendesk value, the resolved name and every category Edvin offered before throwing.
   Decide with ETG which leaf it means (or stop routing it) - do not guess a mapping.
2. **Node 12's action table still uses a `<style>` block, CSS classes and data-* attributes.**
   The parent tree removed all three at its v30 because the org's anti-injection sanitizer
   drops markup after a `<style>` block, which made the whole table - and every selection it
   captured - disappear. Left as-is by request. If the bucket still arrives blank, this is
   the first thing to check: node 27 now logs the raw value it read for each row.
3. **No unresolved-selection guard.** The parent halts a run it cannot resolve (its nodes
   50/51: re-pick, or escalate recording nothing). Here node 27 only flags and logs, so an
   unreadable selection still becomes a silent ticket. Porting the guard also needs a route
   away from the parent's node 44, which throws on an empty final_pnrs.
4. **Passengers.** The parent's passenger screen is skipped on the VI path, so the combined
   record carries only whatever passenger fields the order rows include. If ETG wants named
   passengers on a VI errand, add a passenger Dynamic View before node 1.
5. **Node 1's `type` select still carries the 17 hardcoded Cancellation option labels and
   their `actions_array_name` scores** underneath the dynamic list source. They are dead
   weight for VI (the dynamic source wins) but they are what an agent sees if the dynamic
   list ever fails to load. Clear them or make them the VI type list.

## Changelog

- 2026-08-24 (promotion) - Claude (Cowork)/Brent - Ran etg-env-promote's
  remap-fields.js (sandbox-to-production) alongside the parent tree's promotion.
  Only Contact_Reason (custom_field_29559177650834 -> custom_field_29658558478738,
  2 occurrences) needed remapping in this subtree - 0 skipped, 0 unrecognized,
  0 option-value overrides. Noted for awareness, not touched: this subtree's
  predefined_vars already carried the PRODUCTION Genesys_Conversation ID
  (custom_field_30866832265234) even in the sandbox source, but it's an orphaned
  declaration - 0 real references to either environment's Genesys id anywhere else
  in this tree, so it's inert either way.
  NOT DONE BY THIS SCRIPT - still needs Brent before/at import: re-point CO 182 +
  183 (Get Errand Configurations, node 80 - org_id 116, sandbox) to their
  production-org counterparts, same as the parent tree; confirm the production
  Data Source targets the right Edvin endpoint. This entry only documents the
  remap - not imported anywhere as part of it. nodes: 80 (token remap only), 5
  (this entry)

- 2026-08-21 - Claude/Brent - v7 (rebased onto Brent's 2026-08-21 export, which added the
  self-contained Edvin config fetch at 80/81, the route script at 82 and deleted the 27
  inherited clone nodes): radios -> native dropdowns on 48, 50, 53, 59, 61, 62, 64, 66, 69,
  71, 73, 75, each led by a "- Select -" placeholder; trailing space trimmed from node 71's
  first option so node 72's branch can match. NEW root node 83 builds the COMBINED PNR (all
  selected PNRs joined) as transforms.current_pnr and clears VI state; root_node_id 48 -> 83.
  Node 2 now reads node 81's actions_by_type instead of keeping its own label-only bucket
  mapping (the bucket carry-over fix), captures the VI/STG answers into
  vi_details/vi_details_text and folds them into `notes`, drops the dead CONTACT_REASON
  block, reads `notes` via getVariableValue. Node 27: resolver matches actionId/id/name,
  bucketId carried onto records and tickets, per-row logging of the raw selection,
  unresolved-selection flags. NEW node 84 publishes the finals the parent workflow consumes
  (final_pnrs = [combined record], current_pnr = the same record, plus form-data scalars);
  node 27 continuation 79 -> 84. Node 82 hardened: timezone-free date-only cutoff compare,
  agent-entered orderCreated preferred over the API value, guard + log when neither is
  readable. Node 81 logs the categories Edvin offered before throwing. keep_vars_on_back
  0 -> 1. Stale persistent button (node 29, deleted) cleared. claude.md node rewritten for
  THIS tree - it was still a copy of the parent's.
  nodes 2, 5, 27, 48, 50, 53, 59, 61, 62, 64, 66, 69, 71, 73, 75, 81, 82, 83(new), 84(new),
  tree config
